comments.author: SnowProblem
comments.why: Intro to C4 as a light ruleset for system diagrams
comments.text: If C4 is new to you too, I recommend their intro video: [VIDEO] . It feels like a very light ruleset over what we would do naturally when explaining a system to another engineer. That's great. Some of the ideas that stood out were: 1. Allow flexibility in the notation (shapes and color) as long as the abstractions are good. 2. When drawing arrows, make them unidirectional to show the main intent. 3. Hide details to express the main story (@ 27min in the video) 4. Don't just give names to components. Give short descriptions too. 5. Don't document the lowest levels. Code is better here.

comments.author: tmountain
comments.story: Beyond Whiteboarding: Creating Expert System Architecture Diagrams
comments.why: Introduces C4 model for coherent architecture diagrams
comments.text: These fail my litmus test, which is, "can a third-party look at the diagram and make sense of it without verbal explanation?" For a more formal approach to coherent diagrams and white boarding, I recommend the C4 model. It's conceptually simple and results in better system documentation than the free form method that's commonly used. [VIDEO]
